title: Gather items into a crate
summary: Bring a crate onto a lift, feed five workpieces into it one at a time and send it away full.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Combine a count, a lift and a crate in one sequence of steps.
Move the lift only with its surface stopped, and feed the next workpiece only after the last one has landed.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/LiftStacking.st the inputs and outputs of the station are declared, and the program drives nothing yet. After the press of Start, one crate must come in and ride the lift up to the feeder, five workpieces must be fed into it one at a time, and the full crate must go down and leave on the out belt, with Green lit when OutEye has seen it leave.
stages.checkpoint: You can say what the station is doing at any moment, and what must be true before it goes on to the next job.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the crate and the workpieces: the crate stops on the lift when CrateEye sees it; at level 2 the feeder puts down one workpiece at a time, and each needs a moment to settle in the crate before the next one comes.
stages.checkpoint: The platform's belt never runs while the platform moves, five workpieces enter the crate, and Green lights after OutEye sees the crate leave.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program of the station, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program drives no output, so nothing moves. After Start, one crate must be emitted and brought onto the lift, the lift must raise it, five workpieces must be fed into it one at a time, the lift must lower it and the crate must leave on the out belt, with Green lit when OutEye has seen it.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named lift-stacking and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the workpieces land in the crate in the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}} and read the line "Crate 1 holds … items" in the facts text.
stages.checkpoint: The number in that line rises to five before the crate leaves the lift.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The assertion on loaded:crate:0, which is the number of workpieces resting in the crate, holds as soon as at least one rests inside, and the delivered assertion proves the crate reached its bin.
stages.checkpoint: The grade cannot count the workpieces: it does not tell four from five, because an expectation has no numeric comparison; read the count in the facts.

hints.text: A workpiece is in front of CountEye for a moment and keeps moving after it has gone by. When is it safe to say that this one is done and feed the next? And what keeps the workpieces from piling on one spot of the platform?

Keep an INT Step and a Parts count, latch Start into Active and give EmitCrate the press. Step 1: run RunIn and RunLift until CrateEye sees the crate at AtLevel1. Step 2: Up, with RunLift FALSE, until AtLevel2. Step 3: give EmitPart one rising edge and run the feeder; on the falling edge of CountEye (an F_TRIG) add one to Parts. Step 4: keep the feeder running and wait about two seconds with a TON for the workpiece to land (it settles in about a second). Step 5: run RunLift for 0.3 s so the workpieces do not pile on one spot, then back to step 3, or to step 6 after the fifth. Step 6: Down until AtLevel1. Step 7: run RunLift and RunOut, and light Green on the falling edge of OutEye.

faultCases: The starting program drives no output, so nothing moves.
